newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Low Brazil inflation lifts Sept debt service - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Low Brazil inflation lifts Sept debt service - gov't.

text.p: Low inflation will increase real debt-servicing costs in September but the impact on the Treasury's accounts will be only temporary, the Finance Ministry said Thursday.
The ministry said in its monthly report on economic indicators that it expected real and nominal interest rates to continue their gentle decline.
"According to economic analysts, the recent fall in inflation and subsequent rise in real interest rates will have elevated the costs of public debt this month," it wrote.

"This is true because the stock of debt is not decreasing, which means that the increase in real interest rates corresponds to a higher expenditure on real interest payments. But this is something temporary, which doesn't define a tendency."
The ministry's monthly report on economic indicators, introduced four months ago, does not necessarily reflect "official" views being based on independent market forecasts.
The Gazeta Mercantil newspaper reported Thursday that low inflation could threaten efforts to reduce the fiscal deficit.
August inflation at 0.004 percent as measured by the IGP-DI index has raised real interest rates on internal debt to 1.67 percent in August from 0.68 percent in July, it said.
